notable_absence.finding: Azure region availability is split by a 'Free Tier Support' column, and 6 regions are flagged 'available only on request' (footnote 2) requiring a support ticket to unlock - both are genuine account/region-tier gates with no clean predicate in the registry (requiresSupportPlan is about feature tiers, not per-region availability-on-request). Left unmodeled rather than force-fit onto requiresSupportPlan, since 'available only on request' is a manual provisioning process, not a purchased plan tier.

cross_component_finding: This page contains the batch's single clearest example of the hypothesis's target finding: a Capella feature (Storage Auto-Expansion) that exists identically-named on all three cloud-provider pages, cross-referenced to the identical target section, but whose underlying mechanics are stated to differ specifically under Azure (requires node replacement/rebalancing and causes data movement - a caveat absent from both the AWS and GCP equivalents). This is a genuine within-Capella cloud-provider behavioral difference, not merely an infrastructure spec difference (contrast with the vCPU/memory and disk-type tables, which are pure infra reference). Also worth flagging (known-anomaly recurrence, not new): 'Clusters deployed with Azure use Couchbase Server 7.1 or later, which supports unequal server groups' cites a discrete server/-style version number on a Capella page, the same recurring anomaly seen elsewhere in this and prior batches.
